messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: gpu_capacity_exhaustion detected in aws-ap-south-1. autoscaler failing to provision new GPU nodes; queue depth rising. impact: some Dedicated and Hosted inference routes > 95th pct latency + 429s on enqueue. paging oncall.
raj: Oncall here. Seeing the pager, jumping in. Any immediate customer-facing outages? /cc @support-maya @emma
support-maya: A handful of customers reported elevated errors around 10:42 UTC — mainly high-latency for embedding calls and a few 503s. Not yet full outage but degraded. Ticketing customers now. :grimacing:
emma: I can confirm dashboard shows sustained enqueue growth from 10:38. Autoscaler logs show repeated "insufficient quota" from AWS for request to allocate p4d instances. I'll paste the last lines.
emma: ```
2026-03-15T10:40:12Z autoscaler ERROR allocation failed: AWS::LimitExceeded: You are attempting to allocate more GPUs than your account allows in region ap-south-1. RequestId: abc-123
2026-03-15T10:40:12Z autoscaler INFO retrying allocation x3
2026-03-15T10:41:01Z autoscaler ERROR allocation failed: region quota hit
``` 
lana: Confirmed from AWS console — current GPU quota for our account in ap-south-1 is at limit due to recent onboarding for an enterprise pilot. Quota increase request is open but not approved yet. Request ID 987654321, submitted ~7h ago.
miguel: Queue map: most load is on model-large-gen and emb-v2. emb-v2 latency is spiking, and requests are backing up into long-poll queue. Autoscaler tried to spin up 4 nodes and got blocked.
raj: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Reroute non-critical Hosted traffic to us-east-1 / eu-west-1 model variants; 2) Throttle or shed lower-priority customers; 3) Spin up lower-GPU/CPU fallback variants for embedding (quantized smaller models); 4) Ask infra to request emergency quota bump (we already have request pending).
support-maya: We're tracking customers with priority tags. I'll prepare email templates for affected seats and add to status page.
emma: Trying reroute now for low-priority routes -> failover to us-east-1. I'll flip routing policy for routes tagged "non-prod" and "free-tier" first.
emma: ```
# deploying route change
PATCH /routes/routing-policy
body: {"region_preference": ["us-east-1","eu-west-1","ap-south-1"], "priority_tags": ["free-tier","non-prod"]}
``` 
emma: Change pushed. Non-prod/free-tier traffic now routing to us-east-1. Monitor shows immediate decrease in ap-south-1 enqueue for those tags.
miguel: Good. But embeddings and a few Dedicated tenants still stuck — they can't be rerouted due to data-residency locks.
raj: For dedicated tenants blocked, we can attempt two things: A) Temporarily provision smaller GPU instances within ap-south-1 that don't require new quota (if any left), or B) activate per-tenant degraded mode: reduce concurrency and batch sizes to reduce GPU demand.
lana: Checked instance types: only t4g (CPU) and some older g4 available — nothing matching p4/p3 fleet. Requesting a quota bump for g4/g5 won't help us for high-perf models.
emma: Implementing degraded mode for affected Dedicated pools: lowering max_concurrency by 40% and auto-batching to 16
emma: ```
# config snippet applied to dedicated pool 'ap-south1-dedicated-3'
max_concurrency: 6 -> 4
batch_size_hint: 32 -> 16
fallback_model: model-small-quant
``` 
sre-bot: ALERT: enqueue_depth_ap-south-1 = 312 -> was 28 at 10:30. latency_p99_hosted = 6.2s. CPU-fallback activations: 2 pools.
raj: Also spinning up a temporary routing rule to divert function/tool-calls heavy routes to our cpu-fallback cluster. It will increase latency but avoid 503s.
miguel: Noted. We're at risk of fairness starvation for long-running tenants; need to ensure internal fairness control enforced.
support-maya: Customer comms: initial notification sent for 12 customers in ap-south-1 with potential degradation. They'll get an update once we have ETA for quota increase or full mitigation.
emma: Quick test: triggering a canary request to emb-v2 now — latency dropped from 1.8s to 0.9s for non-prod flow; ap-south-1 still has queuing for pinned tenants.
raj: Can infra attempt a soft emergency allocation by borrowing capacity from partner account? We have a partner spot pool in ap-south-1 under partner-org-2 — need legal ok.
lana: Legal already gave scoped approval for emergency borrowing last quarter — but transfer requires org admin. I'm opening a ticket with cloud-ops to do cross-account allocation. This could take ~15-30m.
emma: Meanwhile, reduce retry backoff on client SDK to avoid thundering retry storms; switch to exponential backoff and jitter.
emma: ```
// sdk config
retries: 2
backoff: exponential(200ms) + jitter
``` 
miguel: Autoscaler logs also show repeated attempts to allocate across AZs within ap-south-1 — all failing due to account-level GPU limit, not AZ capacity.
raj: OK, plan of record:
- Immediate: reroute non-critical routes (done), degraded mode for Dedicated pools (done), SDK retry tuning (in progress).
- Near-term (15-45m): cross-account borrow from partner pool (lana -> cloud-ops), support comms updates (support-maya), continue quota request chase with AWS support (lana).
- Longer-term: request permanent quota increase + add proactive monitoring to surface quota burn earlier.
support-maya: Status page updated: "Degraded performance in AP-South-1; mitigation in progress. Some customers may see higher latency or 429s."
lana: Cloud-ops responded: partner pool eligible; initiating cross-account allocation now. ETA 18m. Will post when instances come up.
raj: Keep small audit note of affected customer IDs and timestamps for postmortem. I'll start the incident doc.
miguel: Also enabling temporary autoscaler fallback to use smaller-GPU instance family in other regions and increase model quantization for embeddings. Pushing a config change.
emma: Pushing final config for degraded pools. Monitoring enqueues. ap-south-1 enqueue trending down slowly.
sre-bot: UPDATE: cross-account allocation succeeded — 4 g4dn.xlarge nodes provisioned and registered to ap-south-1 pool. autoscaler resumed partial scaling. enqueue_depth_ap-south-1 -> 94.
support-maya: Notifying affected customers: update sent, escalation paths included. No increased cancellation risk reported.
raj: Good work team. We'll keep this channel open for 1 hour and then move to postmortem doc. Assigning postmortem leads: miguel (technical), support-maya (customer comms), lana (cloud ops). Any objections?
emma: No objections. I'll capture all logs and attach to the incident doc.
miguel: I'll follow up on quota request escalation and cost impacts for partner borrow.
support-maya: Adding customer replies to the incident doc as they come in.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: gpu_capacity_exhaustion in aws-ap-south-1 -> mitigated (partial). severity lowered to SEV2. Closing pager in 30m if stable.
raj: Thanks everyone. Will reconvene if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
